• gas still warm when measured / leak in apparatus

parts.text: Describe how damp iron wool can be used to find the percentage of oxygen in air.

rows.answer: M1 put damp iron wool at the top of a measuring cylinder / graduated tube
M2 invert in a trough of water and record the initial volume of air
M3 leave for several days until the water level stops rising
M4 measure the final volume; % = decrease ÷ initial volume × 100

parts.text: Describe an investigation to show that iron needs both oxygen and water to rust. Include the expected results.

parts.text: Explain, using examples, how oxidation and reduction can be defined in terms of oxygen and in terms of electrons.

M4 e.g. magnesium + steam → magnesium oxide + hydrogen

parts.text: Describe the tests the student could do to show that the solid is iron(II) sulfate. Give the expected result of each test.

rows.answer:
any six from:
M1 dissolve in water
M2 add sodium hydroxide solution: green precipitate shows Fe²⁺
M3 precipitate turns brown on standing (oxidised)
M4 add dilute hydrochloric acid then barium chloride solution
M5 white precipitate shows sulfate
M6 results together identify iron(II) sulfate
rows.notes: max 6; one mark for each distinct creditworthy point; credit any other valid chemistry relevant to the question; IGNORE repetition of the same point
